title: Six of Shawwal
hookLine: six fasts after Ramadan are like fasting the year (Muslim)

cards: The morning after Eid, the house looks like a party happened: plates in the sink, sweets nobody can face, new clothes hung back up.
For a month the whole rhythm of life was different: the pre-dawn meal, the long afternoon, the date at sunset, the night prayer. Now, suddenly, lunch is back. For some there's relief.

For some, a strange little grief, as if a guest left without saying goodbye. The month after Ramadan is called Shawwal, and tucked into it is a quiet custom: not one more month of fasting, just six more days.

teach.b: The custom rests on a hadith.

In Sahih Muslim, the companion Abu Ayyub al-Ansari reports that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said whoever fasts Ramadan and then follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if they had fasted the whole span of time.
Another report, from the companion Thawban, gives the arithmetic.

teach.h: THIRTY TIMES TEN, PLUS SIX TIMES TEN.
teach.b: A good deed is counted ten times over, a principle the Qur'an itself states. So thirty days of Ramadan count as three hundred, and six more count as sixty. Three hundred and sixty: roughly a year, folded into five weeks.
A few practical things. You don't fast on the day of Eid itself; the Prophet forbade fasting on the two Eids.

teach.h: NOT ON EID; TOGETHER OR SPREAD OUT.
teach.b: After that, the six can be kept back to back, right after Eid, or spread through the month, a Monday here, a Thursday there; scholars have discussed both, and many say either is fine.
People who missed days of Ramadan, through illness, travel, or for women, their monthly period, often ask which comes first, the make-up days or the six.
Here the schools give different answers, and many people simply ask a scholar they trust. Not everyone in early Islam was enthusiastic.
Imam Malik, the scholar of Medina, is reported to have disliked making it a fixed custom, worried people might start treating it as part of Ramadan. Other schools recommend it.

teach.h: KEEP THE DOOR FROM SLAMMING SHUT.
teach.b: For those who keep them, the six keep the door from slamming shut. Ramadan ends, but the habit doesn't vanish overnight; a small part of it stays in the week.

how: Many Muslims fast six voluntary days in Shawwal, the month after Ramadan, starting after the day of Eid; some fast them consecutively and others spread them through the month.

practice: Picture next week and find one calm day, no big dinner, no hard workout.

If you're able, and it's safe for your health, decide to fast it from dawn to sunset; if fasting isn't possible for you, plan to eat one meal that day slowly, with no screen, the way a fast is broken at sunset.
If you pray, you can make your intention quietly now.

wordCard.voice: Shawwal. The month after Ramadan, when many Muslims keep six voluntary fasts that the hadith counts, with Ramadan, as a whole year. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Shawwal, the tenth month of the Hijri year, the month after Ramadan.

carryVoice: Your line: six more. A small piece of Ramadan, kept in the weeks after. Until tomorrow.
